content.text:
Fixed: marked no longer puts a link inside another link. The three examples from the report now give the CommonMark output, e.g. `[foo [bar](/uri)](/uri)` → `

[foo bar](/uri)

`. **Cause:** marked parsed a link's text as normal inline content. If that text contained a complete link (`[bar](/uri)`), the inner link was kept and wrapped in the outer ``. Nothing enforced CommonMark's rule that links can't contain links. **Fix (`src/Lexer.ts`):** - The `link` and `reflink` branches of `inlineTokens` are now one shared branch. - If a resulting `link` token contains another link anywhere inside it, including inside an image, marked drops the outer link. It emits the opening `[` as plain text and carries on parsing from the next character, so the inner link is kept and the outer brackets come out as text. - A new private helper, `containsLink`, does the search. It only counts links written with brackets, so autolinks don't trigger it. - Images are never dropped, because CommonMark allows links inside image descriptions. `[![[foo](/a)](/b)](/c)` now gives `[](/c)`. **Tests:** - I removed the `shouldFail` flags from examples 518, 519 and 532 in both copies of the spec file (`test/specs/commonmark/` and `test/specs/gfm/`), and added a regression test in `test/unit/marked.test.js`. - Spec tests: 1781 passed, 0 failed. Unit tests (all six files): 191 passed, 0 failed. - I couldn't run eslint or `tsc` because permission was denied, so linting and type-checking still need doing. **Still open:** - Example 520 (`![[[foo](uri1)](uri2)](uri3)`) was already marked as an expected failure and still fails. The cause is separate: marked's link pattern only handles one level of brackets inside link text, so it never matches this image. - An autolink inside link text, such as `[](/u)`, still produces nested `` tags. This change deliberately doesn't cover that case.
